findings.description: setTimeout callbacks capture the function-scoped `var i`. By the time they fire the loop has finished and i === jobs.length, so every callback calls run(jobs[jobs.length]) which is undefined. No job is ever run with its real data.
findings.scenario: scheduleJobs(['a','b','c'], run) calls run(undefined) three times instead of run('a'), run('b'), run('c').
findings.fix: Use `for (let i = 0; ...)` so each iteration gets its own binding.

findings.category: wrong sort order and input mutation
findings.description: Array.prototype.sort() without a comparator sorts numbers as strings, so the median is wrong for multi-digit values. It also sorts the caller's array in place.
findings.scenario: median([10, 9, 2]) sorts to [10, 2, 9] and returns 2; the correct answer is 9. The caller's array is also reordered.

findings.description: average divides by values.length with no empty check. The comment says empty input is legitimate for new users, and it yields NaN (0/0).
findings.scenario: average([]) returns NaN, which the dashboard will render or propagate.
findings.fix: if (values.length === 0) return 0; (or null, depending on what the UI expects).

findings.description: median on an empty array computes (sorted[-1] + sorted[0]) / 2, which is NaN. percentile on an empty array returns undefined (sorted[-1]).
findings.scenario: median([]) returns NaN; percentile([], 50) returns undefined. Both are reachable for new users per the comment on line 15.
findings.fix: Return null or 0 early when values.length === 0.
